countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.summary: Kazakhstan is a Central Asian destination for direct-entry medical education, with government-accredited universities offering single-cycle bachelor's-level Medicine programmes recognized by national accreditors such as ECAQA and IAAR and listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools. Almaty and Astana host the country's leading medical faculties.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: A direct-entry medical degree avoids the separate pre-medical bachelor's stage required in some destinations, while national accreditation bodies recognized by the World Federation for Medical Education support international credibility. English-medium tracks are available alongside Kazakh and Russian instruction, and tuition is quoted in Kazakhstani tenge at levels generally below Western destinations.
countries.climate: Continental climate with hot summers and cold winters; Almaty sits near mountain ranges with cooler temperatures than the northern steppe capital Astana, which has some of the coldest winters of any national capital.
countries.metaDescription: Compare Kazakhstan medical universities by tuition, accreditation, admissions, and the direct-entry Medicine route for international students.

universities.name: Al-Farabi Kazakh National University
universities.summary: Al-Farabi Kazakh National University is Kazakhstan's highest-ranked public research university, founded in 1934 in Almaty. Its Faculty of Medicine and Health Care offers a direct-entry Medicine bachelor's degree, nationally accredited by ECAQA through 2030 and listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools, with a dedicated English-medium track alongside Kazakh and Russian instruction.
universities.campusLifestyle: The KazNU campus sits in downtown Almaty, overlooking the Trans-Ili Alatau mountain range, and spans 16 faculties, 64 departments and 8 research institutes. The university ranked around 150th in the QS World University Rankings and around 44th in QS Asia (2023), Kazakhstan's highest-ranked institution. International-student infrastructure includes a dedicated Department of Internationalization and Recruitment and the 'Keremet' Student Service Center.
universities.cityProfile: Almaty, Kazakhstan's largest city and former capital, hosts Al-Farabi Kazakh National University's main campus. The Faculty of Medicine and Health Care is a comparatively newer addition to the century-old university, with WHO directory records showing instruction under its current medical qualification beginning in 2018. International applicants route through a dedicated Department of Internationalization and Recruitment, and the university's 'Keremet' Student Service Center bundles medical, social and psychological-support services on campus.
universities.practicalExposure: The Faculty of Medicine and Health Care runs its own clinical academic department structure, including Departments of Clinical Disciplines, Clinical Specialties, Internal Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Surgery, General Medical Practice, Fundamental Medicine, Stomatology and Nursing, alongside a residency programme spanning more than 20 named clinical specialties such as General Surgery, Cardiology, Ophthalmology, Neurology and Oncology. After the Medicine bachelor's degree, Kazakhstan's system requires a further mandatory one-year clinical Internship programme, listed by the university as a distinct programme code, before a graduate is fully qualified to practice. No specific named external teaching or base hospital is published on the Faculty's official pages; clinical training is described through these named academic-clinical departments and the residency specialty list rather than a single flagship hospital partner.
universities.hostelOverview: KazNU's infrastructure includes on-campus dormitories, but no official, currently-dated per-student dormitory tariff for foreign Medicine students is published on the university's site. Applicants should request current accommodation costs directly from the Department of Internationalization and Recruitment before budgeting.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published for international Medicine students. Daily food and living costs should be planned as a separate budget line, alongside the mandatory medical insurance the university requires for the full period of study and stay in Kazakhstan.
universities.safetyOverview: International students must complete a medical examination under Kazakhstan's migration law and register with the Department of Internationalization and Recruitment within two days of arrival. No separate campus safety statement is published on the university's official pages.
universities.studentSupport: The Department of Internationalization and Recruitment handles foreign-student registration and visa formalities, while the 'Keremet' Student Service Center bundles educational, medical, social and psychological-support services. The Glossa Center and British Educational and Research Center offer Kazakh, Russian and English language-preparation courses.

faq.question: Is Al-Farabi Kazakh National University the same as "Al-Farabi Kazakh National Medical University"?
faq.answer: No -- that name is a common but incorrect third-party label. The correct official name is Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, and its medical degree is housed within the university's own Faculty of Medicine and Health Care, distinct from the separate Asfendiyarov Kazakh National Medical University, also in Almaty.

faq.question: Does the university have a genuine, government-recognized medical degree?
faq.answer: Yes. Its Faculty of Medicine and Health Care's Medicine bachelor's programme is nationally accredited by ECAQA (valid through 2030) and is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools under the qualification title Physician (General Medicine).

faq.question: Is the programme direct-entry from secondary school?
faq.answer: Yes. Per the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools listing, admission follows completion of secondary education, with no separate prior bachelor's degree required.

faq.question: How long is the programme?
faq.answer: The university's own current curriculum page shows 12 semesters (6 academic years). A related, older programme code recorded in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools shows 5 years, so applicants should reconfirm the exact current duration directly with the admissions office.

faq.question: Is teaching available in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The university states that English-medium study in Healthcare requires a certificate of English proficiency and interview-based admission, confirming a genuine English-medium track alongside Kazakh and Russian instruction.

faq.question: What is the 2026-2027 tuition fee for Indian or other foreign students?
faq.answer: Per the university's official fee schedule, the Medicine programme for 'far abroad' foreign nationals (the category applicable to Indian students) is 2,600,000 KZT per year in the English-medium track, or 2,400,000 KZT per year in Kazakh or Russian.

faq.question: When can international students apply?
faq.answer: The university's Foreign Applicants page lists an Autumn intake (documents due 15 May to 20 August) with the academic year typically starting in September; a separate Spring window exists university-wide but is not confirmed as Medicine-specific.

faq.question: Do Indian students still need to meet NEET-UG and NMC requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. India's National Medical Commission Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate Regulations, 2021 require, among other conditions, a minimum 54-month English-medium foreign course plus a 12-month internship at the same institution, followed by India's National Exit Test. Applicants should verify current requirements directly with NMC before enrolling.

faq.question: Is there a dedicated support office for international students?
faq.answer: Yes -- the Department of Internationalization and Recruitment handles foreign-student registration and visa formalities, and the university's 'Keremet' Student Service Center offers medical, social and psychological-support services on campus.

faq.question: What happens after completing the Medicine bachelor's degree?
faq.answer: Kazakhstan's system separately requires a further mandatory one-year clinical internship, listed by the university as a distinct programme, before a graduate is qualified to practice -- applicants should factor this into their total study timeline.

fee.notes: The university's official 2026-2027 tuition schedule, approved by KazNU's Board of Directors (Decision No. 4, 10 July 2026), prices Medicine for 'far abroad' foreign nationals (the category applicable to Indian applicants) at 2,600,000 KZT per year in the English-medium track, or 2,400,000 KZT in Kazakh or Russian. 'Near abroad' CIS-country nationals pay lower rates (2,400,000 / 2,200,000 KZT). Figures are official KZT amounts; any USD conversion is approximate and will fluctuate with the exchange rate.
